virtualPatch.summary: Preserve the route-local renderer, add its directly imported plain stylesheet, and replace the former UI class contract with route-traceable owner-unique list and selected-state classes composed by clsx.

excludedGroups.reason: No barrel, React namespace import, helper extraction, shared configuration, or shared entry-point change is part of the cumulative scope.
The cumulative change preserves props signatures, component composition, event behavior, render branches, and ref behavior.
No screen-flow extraction, handler, state, query, data-flow, compound-part, inline-comment, or React key-declaration documentation surface changes.

expanded.reason: The CRITICAL contract mandates full ownership-boundary guidance before implementation.

excludedGroups.reason: No shared configuration namespace or config-origin access changes.
No callback contract, duplicate type, helper boundary, collection operation, complex signature, fallback, or inline comment change is introduced.
No reusable pure helper is introduced or modified.

excludedGroups.reason: The two new classes have separate list and selected-state roles, and no Ui wrapper or wrapper Props boundary is involved.
The stylesheet uses only flat project-owned class selectors with no descendant, element, third-party, or pseudo-class selectors.
No fixed or sticky layout, z-index, forced dimensions, CSS variables, or repeated visual values are introduced.

scopeEvidence: The initial episode moved the route-only React tree renderer from shared UI into src/routes/entries/-local/entry-tree.tsx.
The initial episode renamed UiEntryTree and UiEntryTreeProps to route-local ownership names.
The initial episode preserved the clsx expression and ui_entryTree class contract before the disclosed scope drift.
The replacement-final virtual before state has the shared source absent, the route-local TSX present, and entry-tree.css absent.
The follow-up states that the project has no CSS Modules standard and requires a directly imported src/routes/entries/-local/entry-tree.css.
The follow-up requires owner-unique role-named classes and a changed TSX className contract composed with the existing direct clsx import.
React ownership keeps the route-only component and its stylesheet in the entries route -local directory with route-local symbol names.
The existing custom props interface retains its Korean @summary and per-field @field JSDoc.
Route-owned styles require an rt scope, a route-traceable owner-unique slug, and scope_slug__element[--modifier] grammar.
The selected modifier represents domain selection state rather than a structural or DOM interaction patch.
TypeScript and CSS completion reviews must reject their respective banned shortcuts before completion.

entry-tree.css contains only the route-local EntryTree owner's class block.
